hero.title: Full-Stack Software Developer
hero.tagline: 3+ years building production systems for supply-chain, warehouse and contact-centre clients — and shipping faster with an AI-assisted workflow.

about.heading: About me
about.body: Full-stack developer with 3+ years of commercial experience in Hong Kong, building and supporting production systems for supply-chain, warehouse and contact-centre clients. Front end in Vue.js, React and React Native; back end in Node.js, Java and Go (Golang); data in Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL and PostgreSQL. Experienced with real-time features (WebSockets / Socket.io), role-based access control, PDF and report generation, and daily production support. I use Claude Code as an AI-assisted development partner — multi-agent workflows, AI code and security review, and scheduled headless runs that verify their own work before committing — to ship faster without lowering the bar.

main.name: Course platform for multiple companies
main.description: A multi-company course platform where each school gets its own URL, teachers manage their own courses, and students scan a QR code to browse a calendar and enrol.
bullets: Built a multi-tenant course platform end to end (React, TypeScript, Express, PostgreSQL): a URL and QR code per school, month-calendar enrolment, cross-school time-conflict checks, three-tier role-based staff management, Google SSO, embedded maps and a Stripe billing skeleton, with the UI in 3 languages.

Designed the scheduling engine: a weekly recurrence rule generates an editable per-session table (move, skip or add single sessions), and a one-click "renew term" carries the settings into the next term.

Hardened the API with per-IP rate limiting, security headers (helmet), fail-fast JWT configuration and user-enumeration protection; an AI-assisted security review found an account-impersonation vulnerability in company registration, which I fixed.
Developed with a Claude Code multi-agent workflow — plan-mode design before implementation, model routing by task complexity — and Playwright end-to-end tests.

Automated recurring work with a weekly headless Claude Code pipeline (launchd): a quota check before each run, a narrow tool allowlist, self-verification with typecheck and build, and commits left unpushed for human review. A six-hourly production check logs every result and records "unreachable" as unreachable rather than reporting a false all-clear.

otto.name: TDS eDOC Project
otto.description: A specialized document management system built on Tradelink's "Trader Documentation Service" platform for a multinational retail sourcing group. It connects an extensive network of supply chain partners — overseas buyers, sellers and freight forwarders — to facilitate, process and optimize multi-national document exchange and workflow automation.
bullets: Developed and maintained core modules of a supply-chain document platform used by overseas buyers, sellers and freight forwarders, and provided daily production support.
Generated standard PDF and XML business documents with JasperReports and XSL-FO.
Wrote cron jobs for scheduled data synchronisation, system housekeeping and log rotation.
Integrated SFTP workflows to automate document transfers from multinational suppliers and forwarders.
Built a barcode / QR code generation module with sequential unit codes (prefix + zero-padded counter) and rollover handling.
Added regex validation to enforce strict field formats (e.g. HS Code length and segment rules).
Implemented role-based access control (RBAC) for create / view / edit / delete / lock permissions across hierarchical accounts and teams.
Created a document template feature so users can save a completed form and reuse it.

kiosk.name: CMHK Kiosk Project
kiosk.description: A warehouse management system (WMS) kiosk application developed for China Mobile Hong Kong (CMHK), deployed across 4 kiosk units for cargo registration and automated inventory control.
bullets: Worked with internal teams and frontline warehouse staff to design and implement features for daily logistics operations.
Built a real-time notification system with Socket.io, connecting client kiosks (receiving / shipping) to warehouse staff units with push notifications and sound alerts.
Handled asynchronous status transitions that lock the kiosk UI while a staff member processes an order, preventing duplicate assignments.
Developed real-time backend verification of scanned QR codes — order data, format and duplicates — against the database.
Implemented an automated quantity check that cross-references scanned items and turns the line green when it matches.
Generated downloadable PDFs, reachable through a system-created QR code, on order completion.
Built a heartbeat mechanism: each kiosk sends its machine ID over a socket every 20 seconds, and an offline unit triggers a red alert.

schedule-tour.title: This is the running product
schedule-tour.body: Six real screens, from the public directory to the admin behind the login. React, Express and PostgreSQL, built end to end.

schedule-tenancy.title: Every school gets its own address
schedule-tenancy.body: A slug in the URL and a QR code on the flyer are all it takes. One codebase, one database, and every query scoped by company — so no school can reach another's data.

schedule-booking.title: A seat is held, or it isn't
schedule-booking.body: The capacity check runs inside a transaction, the teacher's week updates, and Stripe confirms before anything counts as booked. Same API for student, teacher and admin — different scope.

smc-chat.title: A conversation, from the queue to the agent
smc-chat.body: It waits in a queue with the others, an agent takes it, and from then on every line moves on a connection that is already open — inbound and outbound, plus the system notifications nobody asked for. Mid-sentence the agent opens the customer's file: who they are, the last three times they wrote in, and the note being logged against this one.

smc-routing.title: One rule, three different outcomes
smc-routing.body: Conditions are rows in a table — channel, keyword, time of day — and so are the actions they trigger: reply from a template, tag it, send it to a queue. Three conversations fall through the same rule and come out in three places, one of them answered without anybody reading it. Changing who handles what is a setting, not a release.

smc-report.title: The export is cut to who asked for it
smc-report.body: A month of interactions is aggregated in a stored procedure and written out in batches rather than held whole in memory. The download path is built from the requester's authorisation, so a supervisor's file is genuinely shorter than an administrator's — the queues they may not see never reach the disk. Underneath it, a Go service takes the heavy reads straight into the core database.

agents.title: One prompt. A whole team.
agents.body: A dispatcher reads the request, picks one of nine roles, and grades the difficulty — and the grade decides the model. A rename runs on the small one; architecture and security get the big one.

agents-handoff.title: Then it has to pass
agents-handoff.body: Developer hands to tester. Both message files move together or switching language shows raw keys; typecheck and build run before any of it counts as done.

agents-unattended.title: And some of it runs without me
agents-unattended.body: A weekly headless run works a task queue behind a quota probe and a narrow tool allowlist, verifies itself with typecheck and build, then commits — never pushes, so a person reads it first. Another scans the live site every six hours. Both log the quiet weeks too: a monitor you only hear from when it is excited is one you learn to ignore.

otto-desk.title: A document desk for a supply chain
otto-desk.body: A shipment's whole paper trail hangs off one folder — purchase order, packing list, invoice, bill of lading — in a grid that filters down any column, opened from twenty-five document types across sea, air, rail and courier. Drawn, not filmed: the platform is a former employer's, and every folder id, party and number here is invented.

otto-flow.title: A document nobody re-types
otto-flow.body: It arrives over SFTP, opens from a template, is checked against the other documents in its folder, and leaves as PDF and XML on whichever channel that forwarder uses — six of them, plus email. The status track is what everyone watches.

otto-control.eyebrow: Who may touch it, and what it is called
otto-control.title: Permissions and numbers, by rule
otto-control.body: Rights are granted down an account → team → role tree, so an operator can draft but not delete. Document numbers come from a rule — prefix, zero-padded counter, check digit — and the interesting part is what happens when the counter runs out.

kiosk-flow.title: Ninety seconds, standing at a warehouse door
kiosk-flow.body: A driver picks what they are here for, fires a barcode gun at the screen — it types into a hidden field, debounced two seconds — and every code is checked against the WMS before it joins the list. A duplicate is refused. Then a mobile number, and the wait for a human.

kiosk-desk.title: The staff side, and the lock between them
kiosk-desk.body: The check-in is pushed to the warehouse unit with a looping alarm, and arriving outside the booked slot turns it into a decision rather than a formality. Opening the order locks the other kiosk — 'warehouse is busy' — so two people cannot take the same job. Lines go green as the scanners reach the ordered quantity, and a finished order becomes a PDF you take away by QR code.

kiosk-fleet.title: A kiosk that says when it dies
kiosk-fleet.body: Every unit broadcasts its machine id on a twenty-second round, and each one is watching the others. Two silent rounds and it is painted red on every remaining screen — which, in a warehouse where the units are aisles apart, is the only way anyone finds out.

startie-setup.title: An event nobody publishes alone
startie-setup.body: Schedule, registration, form fields, content, awards, theme, menu, FAQ, organiser, announcements — each its own screen. Dates are held against the event's own time zone rather than the server's, and the prize pool adds itself up from however many awards you enter. Submitting hands it to a super admin, and the parts that matter lock until they answer.

startie-money.title: Buying a position, and buying a field
startie-money.body: One tier buys a spot at the top of the listing for a set number of days; the other unlocks the form fields the free plan will not give you. Both go through Stripe Checkout, and neither price is hard-coded — a super admin sets the amount, the days and the discount per tier.

startie-stack.title: Where the request actually goes
startie-stack.body: A Next.js front end holding its state in Recoil, and a NestJS back end reaching PostgreSQL through MikroORM — deployed separately, talking over REST. Uploads go to S3, payments to Stripe, and the JWT is what makes the same endpoint answer a super admin, an event owner and an event joiner differently.

schedule.name: Multi-tenant Course Scheduling Platform
schedule.note: Personal project — the public demo runs on seeded test data, not real schools.
schedule.summary: A multi-tenant course platform: every school gets its own URL and QR code, teachers manage courses and rosters from a company dashboard, and students scan once to browse a month calendar and enrol across schools.
highlights: Multi-tenant by company slug (`/c/:slug`), with a per-company QR code students scan to land straight on the enrolment page — no app install.
Scheduling engine turns a weekly recurrence rule into a concrete, editable session table: reschedule, cancel or restore a single session, or override just that session's location.
Cross-company time-conflict checking, enrolment deadlines and capacity limits, all enforced server-side.
Company role tiers (owner / manager / teacher) with an audit trail recording who changed which course, when, and what the old and new values were.
Google OAuth SSO, JWT + bcrypt auth, per-IP rate limiting and security headers; an AI-driven security review caught an account-impersonation hole in company registration.
Whitelisted branding settings (not raw CSS) let each company and teacher theme their own public page.
Built end-to-end with a Claude Code multi-agent workflow — plan-mode design, model routing by task complexity, and an autonomous pipeline that typechecks, builds and commits.

smc.name: SMC
smc.note: A client's live contact centre — nothing here is a screenshot. Every screen on this page is drawn from the description, and every id, queue, path and figure in it is invented.
smc.summary: A customer engagement and routing system integrated with Genesys Cloud: it assigns communication channels and live agents to chat interactions, answers what it can on its own, and produces the reports the operation is run from.
highlights: Vue.js agent console for live chat, with the conversation queue, the active thread and the customer's file in one view.
WebSockets on both the front end and the back end, carrying chat messages and system notifications in both directions on one open connection rather than a poll.
Agents search, open and log customer profiles and prior interactions without leaving the conversation they are in.
Routing queues configured by trigger condition — channel, keyword, time of day — with automated actions attached: reply from a template, tag, route, or escalate to a person.
Node.js batch export of CSV reports and chat histories, writing in chunks rather than holding the file in memory, with the download path derived from the requester's authorisation.
Admin modules for managing multiple dashboard layouts and UI themes behind the console.
SQL queries and stored procedures in Microsoft SQL Server for system storage and the report aggregations.
A separate Go service exposing high-performance endpoints straight into the core server database, for the reads too heavy to go through the application tier.

PDF and XML business documents generated with JasperReports and XSL-FO.
Cron jobs for real-time data sync, system housekeeping and log rotation.
SFTP workflows automating document transfers from multinational suppliers and forwarders.

kiosk.name: CMHK Kiosk
kiosk.summary: A warehouse management kiosk application for China Mobile Hong Kong, deployed across 4 kiosk units for cargo registration and automated inventory control.
highlights: Real-time notifications over Socket.io connecting client kiosks with warehouse staff units, including sound alerts.
Asynchronous status transitions lock the kiosk UI while a staff member processes an order, preventing duplicate assignments.
Backend verification of scanned QR codes against the database — format, existence and duplicate scans.

Downloadable PDFs generated on order completion, reachable through a system-created QR code.

startie.name: Startie
startie.summary: An event display and management platform: create, edit and publish events, choose from multiple event profile templates, and pay through Stripe for priority listing and premium customization features.
highlights: Three auth roles — super admin, event owner and event joiner — with an admin review / approve / reject flow before an event goes public.
Event dashboard covering schedule, activities, descriptions, requirements and FAQ, built on react-hook-form.
Rich text via ckeditor5-react for event descriptions and profile content.
react-timezone-select to keep dates accurate when the backend runs in a different time zone.
Stripe Checkout integration for VIP plans and paid customization features.
Unlimited custom tags, target groups and awards, with automatic prize-pool totals.
Three selectable profile templates plus cover image uploads; per-event reports for visitors, comments and submissions.
Next.js frontend with Recoil for global state, talking to an MVC backend over a RESTful API.
